Dennis Rader (born March 9, 1945) is an American serial killer who murdered ten people around Wichita, Kansas, between 1974 and 1991. While his victims were mostly adult females he also killed males and both children and adults.

He is known as the BTK killer which stands for "Bind, Torture, Kill", which he named himself after the way that he would torture and murder his victims. He sent letters describing the details of the killings to police and local news outlets during the interval in which the murders took place.

After a long hiatus in the 1990s through early 2000s, Rader resumed sending letters in 2004. In his final letter to police he asked if his writings, if put on a floppy disk, could be traced or not. The police answered his question in a newspaper ad posted in the Wichita Eagle saying it would be safe to use the disk.

Rader subsequently sent a 1.44-MB floppy disk on which police found metadata on a Microsoft Word document that showed the program was registered to "Christ Lutheran Church", and the document was marked as last modified by "Dennis". An internet search determined that a Dennis Rader was president of the church council. After confirming his connection through secret DNA collection, Rader was arrested and subsequently pled guilty. He is currently serving 10 consecutive life sentences at El Dorado Correctional Facility in Kansas.
